walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 2: Poetry and Prose Texts and Imaginative Writing — a core area of GCSE English Language.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Poetry and Prose Texts and Imaginative Writing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 2: Poetry and Prose Texts and Imaginative Writing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is a speech act according to Searle/Austin?
options: RP is the accent everyone in southern England uses.
An utterance that performs an action — promising, ordering, apologising, declaring. Speech acts have locutionary (what's said), illocutionary (intended force) and perlocutionary (effect) dimensions.
A speech act is a performance or a play.
A speech act is any time someone speaks.

mcqs.q: What is convergence in accommodation theory?
options: Convergence is when two speakers start using identical accents permanently.
RP is the accent everyone in southern England uses.
Convergence means two languages merge into one new language.
When a speaker adjusts their speech to be more similar to their interlocutor's — to express solidarity, gain approval or ease communication.
